cemc-galois-2009-01a.title: Fraction of the class
cemc-galois-2009-01a.body:
There are $8 + 7 + 3 + 2 = 20$ students, 8 of them blonde: $\frac{8}{20} \times 100\% = 40\%$.

**Answer: 40%**

cemc-galois-2009-01b.title: Fraction of the class
cemc-galois-2009-01b.body:
$3 + 2 = 5$ of the 20 students have red or black hair: $\frac{5}{20} \times 100\% = 25\%$.

**Answer: 25%**

cemc-galois-2009-01c.title: The class size stays 20
cemc-galois-2009-01c.body:
Dyeing hair doesn't change the class size of 20. For 20% to have black hair we need $0.2 \times 20 = 4$ students with black hair. There are 2 now, so 2 blonde students must dye their hair black.

**Answer: 2**

cemc-galois-2009-01d.title: Equation
cemc-galois-2009-01d.body:
If $x$ red-haired students join, $\frac{3 + x}{20 + x} = \frac{32}{100} = \frac{8}{25}$. Then $75 + 25x = 160 + 8x$, so $17x = 85$ and $x = 5$.

**Answer: 5 students**

cemc-galois-2009-01d.title: Count the others
cemc-galois-2009-01d.body:
The $8 + 7 + 2 = 17$ students who are not red-haired never change. If red-haired students make up 32%, these 17 make up 68% of the class, so the class has $17 \div 0.68 = 25$ students: $25 - 20 = 5$ must join.

**Answer: 5 students**

cemc-galois-2009-02a.title: Same move along parallel sides
cemc-galois-2009-02a.body:
In square $ABCD$, going from $D$ to $C$ is the same move as going from $A$ to $B$: 6 right and 3 down. So $C = (3 + 6, 3 - 3) = (9, 0)$ and $t = 9$.

**Answer: $t = 9$**

cemc-galois-2009-02a.title: Parallel slopes
cemc-galois-2009-02a.body:
$AB$ has slope $\frac{6 - 9}{12 - 6} = -\frac12$. $DC \parallel AB$, so $\frac{0 - 3}{t - 3} = -\frac12$, giving $t - 3 = 6$ and $t = 9$.

**Answer: $t = 9$**

cemc-galois-2009-02b.title: Intersect the two lines
cemc-galois-2009-02b.body:
Line $OD$ passes through $(0,0)$ and $(3,3)$: $y = x$.

Line $AB$ has slope $-\frac12$ and passes through $B(12, 6)$: $6 = -6 + b$, so $y = -\frac12 x + 12$.

Setting $x = -\frac12 x + 12$ gives $\frac32 x = 12$, $x = 8$. So $E = (8, 8)$.

cemc-galois-2009-03a.title: Height by Pythagoras
cemc-galois-2009-03a.body:
The altitude bisects the base, giving a right triangle with hypotenuse 2 and leg 1. The height is $\sqrt{4 - 1} = \sqrt3$. Area $= \frac12 (2)(\sqrt3) = \sqrt3$.

**Answer: $\sqrt3$**

cemc-galois-2009-03a.title: Formula
cemc-galois-2009-03a.body:
An equilateral triangle with side $s$ has area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2 = \frac{\sqrt3}{4} \cdot 4 = \sqrt3$.

**Answer: $\sqrt3$**

cemc-galois-2009-03b.title: Six equilateral triangles
cemc-galois-2009-03b.body:
Joining the centre to the six vertices cuts the hexagon into 6 triangles. Six $60^\circ$ angles fill the $360^\circ$ around the centre, and the triangles' angles at the vertices give $60^\circ + 60^\circ = 120^\circ$, the interior angle of a regular hexagon; so the hexagon is exactly six equilateral triangles of side 2.

Area $= 6\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $6\sqrt3$**

cemc-galois-2009-03b.title: Rectangle plus two triangles
cemc-galois-2009-03b.body:
A regular hexagon of side 2 splits into a central rectangle $2 \times 2\sqrt3$ (the distance between opposite vertices across is $2\sqrt3$) and two isosceles triangles with base $2\sqrt3$ and height 1. Area $= 4\sqrt3 + 2 \cdot \frac12 (2\sqrt3)(1) = 6\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $6\sqrt3$**

cemc-galois-2009-03c.title: Add and subtract sectors
cemc-galois-2009-03c.body:
Each interior angle of the hexagon is $120^\circ$.

- At $B$, $D$, $F$ the unshaded sectors inside the hexagon have angle $120^\circ$: each is $\frac13$ of a unit circle, area $\frac{\pi}{3}$; total $\pi$.
- At $A$, $C$, $E$ the shaded sectors outside the hexagon have angle $360^\circ - 120^\circ = 240^\circ$: each $\frac23 \pi$; total $2\pi$.

Shaded area $= 6\sqrt3 - \pi + 2\pi = 6\sqrt3 + \pi \approx 13.53$.

**Answer: $6\sqrt3 + \pi$**

cemc-galois-2009-03c.title: Move the bites
cemc-galois-2009-03c.body:
Each $120^\circ$ bite removed at $B$, $D$, $F$ can be matched against $120^\circ$ of the $240^\circ$ bulge at $A$, $C$, $E$; what is left over is three extra $120^\circ$ sectors, i.e. one full unit circle in total: area $\pi$. So the shaded area is the hexagon plus $\pi$: $6\sqrt3 + \pi$.

**Answer: $6\sqrt3 + \pi$**

cemc-galois-2009-04a.title: Take every coefficient as large as possible

cemc-galois-2009-04c.title: Repeated division with remainder
Counting argument
cemc-galois-2009-04c.body: There are $2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5 \cdot 6 = 720$ choices of $(a, b, c, d, e)$, and each gives a value between 0 and 719. If two different choices gave the same value, look at the largest index $k$ where they differ, say the coefficients there differ by at least 1. Then the difference of the two values is at least $k! - \sum_{j<k} j \cdot j! = k! - (k! - 1) = 1 > 0$ in absolute value — a contradiction. So the 720 choices give 720 different values in $\{0, \dots, 719\}$, i.e. every value. ∎

cemc-galois-2009-04d.title: Split into two independent parts
cemc-galois-2009-04d.body:
With $c = 0$: $n = (a + 2b) + 24(d + 5e)$.

- $n_1 = a + 2b$ takes each value $0, 1, \dots, 5$ exactly once.
- $n_2 = d + 5e$ takes each value $0, 1, \dots, 29$ exactly once.

So the numbers are $n_1 + 24 n_2$, one for each of the $6 \times 30 = 180$ pairs, all different. Their sum is

$$30(0 + 1 + \dots + 5) + 6 \cdot 24 (0 + 1 + \dots + 29) = 30 \cdot 15 + 144 \cdot 435 = 450 + 62640 = 63090.$$

**Answer: 63090**

cemc-galois-2009-04d.title: Average times count
cemc-galois-2009-04d.body:
There are $2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 6 = 180$ choices of $(a, b, d, e)$. Each coefficient takes each of its values equally often, so the average of $n$ is $\frac12(1) + 1(2) + 2(24) + \frac52 (120) = 0.5 + 2 + 48 + 300 = 350.5$. (No two choices give the same $n$, by the uniqueness of the representation.) Sum $= 180 \times 350.5 = 63090$.

**Answer: 63090**
